overview: The MPS High School Building Committee convenes to manage and execute the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) building project for Medford High School. Commencing its inaugural meeting in May 2024, the committee guided the project through early eligibility requirements, project management procurement, design team selection, and feasibility studies. Across its meeting history, the committee systematically evaluated dozens of building options, space efficiency proposals, site layouts, and mechanical systems. Following the selection of a preferred schematic design, the committee finalized space reductions and selected a Construction Manager at Risk to advance the project toward its next design phase. At its most recent meeting in October 2026, the committee approved contract negotiations with Suffolk as Construction Manager at Risk, adopted mechanical and solar recommendations, and established a revised total project cost estimate of approximately $699 million.

threads.name: Owner's Project Manager (OPM) Selection
threads.summary: In mid-2024, the committee initiated preparation for procuring an Owner's Project Manager (OPM) under MSBA Module 2 requirements [M07#3]. An OPM Selection Committee was formed in September 2024 [M08#4], leading to the drafting and approval of a Request for Services detailing evaluation criteria and project scope [M09#1, M10#3]. Left Field was formally introduced and selected as the project's OPM in May 2025 [M11#2]. The committee subsequently approved the official contract for Left Field in June 2025 following MSBA review [M12#2].

threads.name: Designer Procurement and Architectural Team Selection
threads.summary: The committee approved a draft Request for Services in May 2025 to initiate the search for a project designer [M11#3]. After reviewing the MSBA selection schedule and evaluation criteria [M13#2, M14#1], the committee evaluated four design proposals submitted by firms including DLR, Perkins&Will, AI3, and SMMA in September 2025 [M15#4]. SMMA was ranked as the top firm by the Designer Selection Panel [M16#2]. In November 2025, the committee formally approved the feasibility study contract with SMMA [M17#3].

threads.name: Building Design Options and Feasibility Alternatives
threads.summary: The project team presented 29 initial conceptual design options in January 2026 covering code upgrades, renovations, and new construction [M23#6], which were compiled into the Preliminary Design Program submitted to the MSBA [M27#3]. To meet an expedited state timeline, the committee evaluated options against a scoring matrix and narrowed the alternatives down to six finalists in March 2026 [M32#2, M34#4]. In May 2026, a 1967 deed restriction forced the elimination and reconfiguration of several concepts [M48#2]. The committee voted in June 2026 to select Option C2.2A as the preferred schematic design [M52#10] and authorized the Preferred Schematic Report submission to the MSBA [M54#3].

threads.name: Construction Manager at Risk Procurement
threads.summary: Early feasibility documents noted the potential use of a Construction Manager at Risk delivery method [M09#2]. In June 2026, a dedicated subcommittee reviewed procurement guidelines and authorized the drafting of a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) [M53#1, M53#10], which was approved by the full committee [M54#4]. Following proposal reviews and ranking, the committee voted in October 2026 to enter formal contract negotiations with top-ranked firm Suffolk to serve as Construction Manager at Risk [M66#3, M67#3].

threads.name: Space Summary, Vocational Expansion, and Project Cost Reductions
threads.summary: The committee early on studied expanding Chapter 74 vocational programs and aligning building square footage with state guidelines [M03#4, M05#3]. Detailed space summaries were developed comparing existing facilities to MSBA templates, accounting for expanded CTE requirements [M20#5, M29#1]. As preliminary cost estimates exceeded initial projections, the committee established formal space reduction procedures in April 2026 [M45#4]. Subsequent approvals systematically trimmed square footage across administrative, athletic, auditorium, academic, and vocational spaces [M58#9, M62#8, M66#5]. By October 2026, cumulative space efficiency decisions lowered the estimated total project cost to approximately $699 million [M66#5, M67#12].

threads.name: Sustainability, Energy, and Mechanical Systems
threads.summary: Initial design kickoff targeted MSBA reimbursement bonuses by adhering to specialized stretch codes and LEED standards [M16#5, M19#2, M24#6]. Environmental modeling included a 50-year Life Cycle Cost Analysis comparing geothermal ground-source, air-to-water heat pump, and hybrid HVAC systems [M49#6, M56#6]. In September 2026, the advisory team recommended an all-electric 100% air-to-water heat pump system over geothermal options due to lower upfront costs and technical feasibility [M63#4]. The committee formally adopted the air-to-water heat pump system alongside a 100% solar Power Purchase Agreement for roof and parking canopy photovoltaics in October 2026 [M65#1, M66#4].

threads.name: Community Engagement, Advisory Teams, and Public Outreach
threads.summary: A Communications and Community Engagement subcommittee was established at the inaugural meeting to manage public outreach, surveys, and website development [M01#4, M02#4, M03#3]. In late 2025, the committee launched four specialized advisory teams—Sustainability, Safety, Design, and Equity—to gather stakeholder input [M17#7, M21#7]. Outreach efforts expanded in 2026 to include multi-lingual community forums, citywide mailers, and student-produced videos [M25#2, M34#3]. The committee and advisory groups continued hosting public forums through September 2026 to collect feedback on climate, energy, and site plans [M60#1].

Top-ranked design firm SMMA kicked off the feasibility study phase, leading educational visioning and site investigations [M16#2, M16#3, M17#5]. The committee hosted community forums, reviewed 29 conceptual design alternatives, and submitted the Preliminary Design Program to the MSBA [M21#1, M23#6, M27#3]. Members updated evaluation criteria and selected six design options to move forward for detailed study [M27#4, M34#4].

periods.narrative: The committee advanced schematic design work, receiving positive feedback from the MSBA on its educational plan [M55#4, M57#4]. Members approved substantial space efficiency reductions across academic, vocational, and community programs to manage costs and voted to proceed with renovating the base pool facility [M58#9, M59#5, M62#8, M62#9].

The committee voted to enter contract negotiations with Suffolk as Construction Manager at Risk and adopted recommendations for an air-to-water heat pump HVAC system and solar PPA [M66#3, M66#4]. Final space adjustments lowered the estimated total project cost to approximately $699 million [M66#5, M67#12].
